pr_title: Ensure FileStatus and FileSystemEntry Hidden and ReadOnly attributes are retrieved the same way
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/37301

These two files do very similar tasks, but when it comes to collect the Hidden attribute, the first one is simpler than the second one:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/bd6cbe3642f51d70839912a6a666e5de747ad581/src/libraries/System.IO.FileSystem/src/System/IO/Enumeration/FileSystemEntry.Unix.cs#L59-L67

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/bd6cbe3642f51d70839912a6a666e5de747ad581/src/libraries/System.IO.FileSystem/src/System/IO/FileStatus.Unix.cs#L81-L82

This change ensures both collect the Hidden attribute the same way, and makes it more obvious that both methods are closely related.

Also, the ReadOnly attribute was not being collected in the first file, so I added code to do it, as well as a unit test.

I ran all the System.IO.FileSystem unit tests in Ubuntu and in MacOS and they passed. Pending yet to see the CI results.

This fix needs to go into 5.0, or later it could become a breaking change, as explained [here](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/37301#issuecomment-649209428).
pr_comments: @iSazonov can you take a look to this PR? I think I still need to add code to throw but I'm not entirely sure exactly where.

@Jozkee @iSazonov can you take another look? The new commits include:
- Added unit tests for each platform, and split an existing one into platforms: The `FileAttributes.Hidden` flag is only supported by Windows and MacOS. Linux does not support it, the file needs to be hidden using a dot prefix in the filename.
- I found a bug in the `FileSystemEntry.IsHidden` property, where we were only checking for the dot prefix in the filename, but we also had to check for the `IsHidden` attribute.
- Cleaned the code as suggested in the PR.

Thanks for fixing this!

What is Preview we get the fix in?

issue_context.title: FileSystemEntry.Attributes property is not correct on Unix
issue_context.body:
<!--This is just a template - feel free to delete any and all of it and replace as appropriate.-->

### Description

Comes from https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/pull/12834 where custom file enumerator is replaced with .Net FileSystemEnumerator.

_Expectation is that:_
1. FileSystemEntry.Attributes property works the same as FileSystemInfo.Attributes property for Hidden (and perhaps ReadOnly) flags.
2. For Extended Unix flags and Windows Reparse points we need new property FileSystemInfo.ExtendedAttributes.


It turns out the first has a simplified implementation 
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/bd6cbe3642f51d70839912a6a666e5de747ad581/src/libraries/System.IO.FileSystem/src/System/IO/Enumeration/FileSystemEntry.Unix.cs#L69-L84

than the second 
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/bd6cbe3642f51d70839912a6a666e5de747ad581/src/libraries/System.IO.FileSystem/src/System/IO/FileStatus.Unix.cs#L76-L91

Also CHFLAGS works only on BSD-like systems (MacOS, FreeBSD) but not on Linux. So expectation is that assigning Hidden flag on Linux throws PlatformNotSupportedException - it was very amazing to discover that some PowerShell tests are passed on Linux but really Hidden flag does not work.
comments: Was this just an oversight in https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/pull/34560
@davidkaya @danmosemsft @JeremyKuhne Could you please look the issue? I'd be happy to get the fix for PowerShell.

@danmosemsft Yes, this looks like an oversight. We should add a comment in both places pointing out the connection if we can't share the code.

@iSazonov I'm no longer on the libraries team, but this should clearly be consistent between the two. @carlossanlop will have to decide the best course of action on throwing. If we can be confident on checking that it isn't supported than throwing seems reasonable to me at first glance.
If the fix is "to throw" the issue should be fixed in 5.0 milestone - later it will be a breaking change.
@iSazonov I marked it for 5.0. Would you have a chance to work on this in the next few days? If not, @Jozkee or I can take over when we get some bandwidth.
@carlossanlop I have not possibility to develop on Unix :-(
@danmosemsft I would like, but my laptop is against  😃
@iSazonov can you take a look at [the PR](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/40641), please?

> Priority:3

I wonder how you weight this:
1. There is two code paths which contradict each other
2. There is a clear performance issue
3. Finally, it's just bad design, even wrong

@iSazonov Thanks for the comment and feedback. The priority is based on our overall themes and the relative priority of fixing this issue compared to completing other items that the team is committing to for 6.0.0. Even with `Priority:3`, our project plan includes time to work on this issue during the 6.0.0 release cycle.

@jeffhandley Thanks for clarify! I am trying to speed up PowerShell Core file operation and I hope we get this in the PowerShell milestone. So I have many concerns about .Net file API design and performance. Feel free to ping me when will your team start this work.
@iSazonov What timing would enable you to utilize this fix in the PowerShell milestone you're targeting?
@jeffhandley MSFT PowerShell team said they want to stop big changes before summer and then work only on bugs and stability.

~I added in the OP that is right design should be - "For Extended Unix flags and Windows Reparse points we need new property FileSystemInfo.ExtendedAttributes."~

Update: It should be File Flags. Extended Attributes is another conception.

review_comments: Can you also add an OSX test that uses the dot prefix?
The test `IsHiddenAttribute_Unix` in line 127 runs in OSX too (`TestPlatforms.AnyUnix` is `true` in OSX).

It is better move p/invokes from FileSystemEntry.Initialize() in the place and exclude re-reading too.
The same for all attributes.
I talked to @Jozkee about this, we can get them moved to a separate helper class, but I would like to do that in a future PR.
Should we think about performance and initialize these attributes lazy? It would be great for file enumeration.
Not for this change, but we can make the improvement in the future.
No, it needs to be accessed by `FileSystemEntry` too, which is in the same assembly.

No changes in this test, just organized some lines for easier understanding.
It also helps to show that this test is affected by my PR.

EDIT: I actually ended up making changes in this file, to split the tests into each platform, since the IsHidden property is not supported in Linux.
Why do we re-read if we have Refresh() for this.

I'm not sure I understand the question.

The functionality of this code has not been changed. I merely moved the contents of the old `IsReadOnly` method into its own internal helper static method that can be accessed by both `FileSystemEntry` and `FileStatus`, to avoid repeating code.

I don't think we should do a `Refresh` call here, that's what `EnsureStatInitialized` is for - it will only perform a `Refresh` if we haven't called it yet.
As for throw, in line 131 below Hidden attribute presents as valid - I think we could exclude it on systems which do not support this. (I don't know how detect this in right way.)
If `FileAttribute.Hidden` is not supported on Linux, we should update the  docs since they say otherwise https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.io.fileattributes?view=netcore-3.1

I'm not convinced we have to throw for this.

If the flag is not supported in the current OS, then it will never be set, so any condition checking if the UF_HIDDEN flag was set, will be false.
